item.title: Show HN: QuickPing - dead simple way for customers to get in touch with you (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: I got tired of creating a new email account, or setting up (and paying for) a Google Workspace every time I launched a side project. All I wanted was a link I could put on my site that lets someone send me a message and have a conversation. QuickPing gives you a shareable URL (like quickping.dev/to/yourproject). Someone visits it, types their name, email, and a message. You get notified and reply from a dashboard. They get an email with a link back to the thread. No chat widget, no embed code. Just a link you add to your site. Built with Next.js, Neon, and Mailgun. I'm using it for QuickPing's own contact page. https://quickping.dev Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48812731 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

item.title: Show HN: Mandelbrot set renderer written in pure [BSD] Makefiles (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: No calls to shell, no external binaries executed, just pure [BSD] Makefiles rendering my favorite fractal. bmake (AKA BSD make) is the implementation of make(1) used by BSD operating systems. It does not support basic arithmetic, it doesn't have infinite loops, no floating point support, but I forced it to render a fractal anyways :) . To use BSD make on Linux, search your package manager for "bmake", install it, and run `bmake` inside the cloned repo instead of `make`. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48812530 Points: 2 # Comments: 0
